messages.subject: A problem with CFI / TLI
parts:
Hi guys,
I came across a problem with lavaan. Please find attached a dataset containing 19 variables which are almost completely uncorrelated. Cronbachs alpha =-.02. Nonetheless, if running a one-dimensional CFA in lavaan, I get a Comparative Fit Index of 1 and a TLI of 1.298.
This must be some sort of bug, or am I not getting it?
Martin

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: A problem with CFI / TLI
parts:
CFI and TLI as measures of lack of fit. When your observed variables are essentially uncorrelated, then most any model will fit well, if you can get the estimation to converge. Lack of fit is a matter of failing proportionality constraints, and with a bunch of zeroes, proportionality constraints fit just fine. Plus, even with large n, you likely lack the power to detect the lack of fit.

CFI is simple. Chi-square is less than DF for the target model, so the noncentraily estimate is 0. CFI is 1 - (target noncentrality / baseline noncentrality), so it is 1 basically by default. That is, your target model fit is essentially perfect.

For TLI, the formula is more involved, but the result is correct.
TLI = ((chibase/df) - (chitarget/df)) / ((chibase/df) - 1)

Some people interpret TLI > 1 as indicating overfitting. Case in point.
